content:
# AIUI WXSS Reference

This file documents the currently confirmed WXSS and CSS support surface for AIUI agents.

- Treat this file as the source of truth for selector and property support when generating styles.
- Only use selectors and properties that are explicitly listed here.
- Do not infer browser-level CSS compatibility beyond the confirmed support surface.

## Confirmed Selector Support

Only the following selector categories are currently documented as supported:

- **Class selector**: `.class`
- **ID selector**: `#id`
- **Type selector**: `element`, such as `view` and `text`
- **Grouping combinator**: `A, B`
- **Descendant combinator**: `A B`
- **Child combinator**: `A > B`
- **Documented pseudo-classes**: `:active`, `:hover`, `:focus`, `:first-child`, `:last-child`, `:nth-child(n)` (including `odd` / `even`), and `:disabled`.
- **Generated text boxes**: `::before` / `::after` on single-line `<text>` only; see [animation](./animation.md#generated-text-decorations).

Authoring rules:

- Prefer class selectors for most styling work.
- Use ID selectors sparingly for targeted hooks.
- Use type selectors only when the rule truly applies to all instances of a component tag.
- Do not generate selector categories that are not listed in this file.

## Confirmed Layout Properties

### Flexbox

Confirmed Flexbox-related properties:

- `display: flex`
- `flex-direction`
- `flex-wrap`
- `justify-content`
- `align-items`
- `flex-grow`
- `flex-shrink`
- `flex-basis`
- `flex`
- `gap`
- `row-gap`
- `column-gap`

### Grid

Confirmed Grid-related properties:

- `display: grid`
- `grid-template-columns`
- `grid-template-rows`
- `grid-auto-columns`
- `grid-auto-rows`
- `grid-auto-flow`
- `grid-column`
- `grid-column-start`
- `grid-column-end`
- `grid-row`
- `grid-row-start`
- `grid-row-end`
- `grid-area`
- `align-content`
- `justify-items`
- `align-self`
- `justify-self`
- `gap`
- `row-gap`
- `column-gap`

### Sizing And Spacing

Confirmed box model and sizing properties:

- `width`
- `height`
- `margin`
- `padding`
- Their individual `-top`, `-right`, `-bottom`, and `-left` forms.
- `box-sizing`

### Positioning And Overflow

Confirmed positioning and overflow properties:

- `position`: supports `static`, `relative`, `absolute`, and `fixed`
- `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`, and `z-index`
- `display: none` and `overflow: hidden`

Layout authoring rules:

- Prefer Flexbox when either Flexbox or Grid can satisfy the layout.
- Use Grid only when the UI needs coordinated row and column placement.
- Keep layouts simple and predictable for wearable-sized interfaces.

## Confirmed Styling Properties

### Colors And Backgrounds

Confirmed color and background properties:

- `color`
- `background-color`
- `background-position`
- Custom properties such as `--token-name`
- `var(--token-name)` references

### Borders And Outlines

Confirmed border and outline properties:

- `border`
- `border-width`
- `border-style`
- `border-color`
- `border-radius`
- Independent `border-top`, `border-right`, `border-bottom`, and `border-left`, including each side's width, style, and color longhands.
- `outline`
- `outline-width`
- `outline-style`
- `outline-color`
- `outline-offset`

### Typography

Confirmed typography properties:

- `font-size`
- `line-height`
- `font-weight`
- `font-family`
- `font-style`
- `text-align`
- `white-space: nowrap` with a constrained width, `overflow: hidden`, and `text-overflow: ellipsis` for single-line truncation. This does not provide multiline clamping.

### Effects And Visibility

Confirmed visual effect properties:

- `opacity`
- `visibility`
- `box-shadow`
- `filter`
- `transform`
- `transform-origin`
- Independent 2D `translate`, `rotate`, and `scale`; see [animation](./animation.md#2d-transforms-and-interpolation) for supported functions and composition.

### Motion

Confirmed transition and animation properties:

- `transition`
- `transition-property`
- `transition-duration`
- `transition-timing-function`
- `transition-delay`
- `animation`, `animation-name`, `animation-duration`, `animation-timing-function`, `animation-delay`, `animation-iteration-count`, `animation-direction`, and `animation-fill-mode`

Read [animation.md](./animation.md) for concurrent keyframes, timing, animation
events, and text-triggered replay. Generated-text properties `content`,
`event-trigger`, `animation-trigger`, and `-ink-animation-trigger-instance-limit`
are limited to that documented feature.

Styling authoring rules:

- Prefer theme tokens through `var(--token-name)` over hardcoded colors, spacing, radii, and border widths.
- Keep custom property names semantic and local to the feature when introducing new tokens.
- Prefer production-safe styles over browser-specific techniques.

## Other Confirmed WXSS Features

The following WXSS features are also confirmed:

- `@import` can be used to import external style sheets.
- Media queries are used in the sample capability pages and are part of the confirmed authoring surface.
- `@keyframes` defines animations; `@font-face` loads custom fonts.
- `!important` participates in cascade priority, including overriding keyframe values.

After `@import`, combine classes with `class="container flex-center"` in WXML;
`composes` is unsupported.

## Calculated and Random Values

`calc()` accepts exactly two operands with `+` or `-` and spaces around the
operator. Use compatible lengths (for example `calc(100vw - 20px)`) or two
percentages. Sizes, margin / padding / gap, and insets accept these values.
Multiplication, division, nesting, and mixing percentages with lengths such as
`width: calc(100% - 20px)` are unsupported for ordinary sizing and spacing.

Experimental `random()` supports these forms:

```css
.spark {
  opacity: 0.8;
  opacity: random(0.4, 1);
  margin-left: 0;
  margin-left: random(-20px, 20px, 5px);
  animation-duration: 700ms;
  animation-duration: random(400ms, 1s, 100ms);
  width: 6px;
  width: random(--size, 4px, 10px, 2px);
  height: 6px;
  height: random(--size, 4px, 10px, 2px);
}
```

- Syntax is `random([auto | --key,] min, max[, step])`. Use literal fallbacks before experimental declarations.
- Bounds must be compatible literal numbers, lengths, percentages, or times; optional step must be positive and compatible. Discrete values are `min + n * step`, including the upper bound only when a step lands on it. If `max < min`, the result is `min`.
- The consuming property determines the accepted type and limits. Length units can mix, as can `ms` / `s`; percentages cannot mix with lengths or numbers.
- Values remain stable across style recomputation. A named key shares a random base within an element: equal ranges/steps yield equal values; different ranges map that base to their own range. Values do not share across elements.
- Animation endpoints are resolved before interpolation and remain stable during playback. Each triggered replay gets a fresh context without changing older retained instances.
- Nested `calc()` / `random()` arguments, random angles/frequencies/resolutions, cross-element sharing, `element-shared`, and fixed random sources are unsupported. Invalid expressions invalidate the declaration. Use Web Crypto for secure randomness.

## Explicitly Unsupported Or Not Implemented

The following constraints are explicitly called out by the current repository and should be treated as unsupported for generated code:

- Browser-only CSS behavior is unsupported unless AIUI explicitly documents it.
- Unsupported CSS shorthands beyond the confirmed support surface must not be assumed to work.
- `position: sticky` is not supported.
- `animation-play-state`, 3D transforms, and perspective are unsupported.
- `font-variant` is not supported.
- `word-break` is not supported.
- Browser `::placeholder`, `::-webkit-scrollbar`, and generated boxes on arbitrary containers or multiline `<text>` are outside the supported subset. Use component placeholder properties.
- Any selector category or property not listed in this file is outside the confirmed support surface and must not be generated by default.

## Authoring Rules For Agents

- Treat this file as implementation truth, not browser truth.
- Generate only the selectors and properties listed here.
- Prefer class-based styling and semantic theme tokens.
- Keep WXSS concise, deterministic, and easy to render on wearable layouts.

title: AIUI Development
content:
---
name: "aiui-dev"
description: "Develop and debug AIUI agents, Pages, Widgets, Agent Workers, built-in components, WXSS, and runtime APIs. Use when generating or reviewing AIUI .ink, app.json, page logic, UI, or API integrations."
---

# AIUI Development

Build AIUI agents from the current contracts in this skill. Do not assume an API, component, CSS property, browser behavior, or lifecycle merely because it exists on the Web or in WeChat Mini Programs.

## Load Only What the Task Needs

- Read [framework.md](./references/framework.md) for project structure, `app.json`, Page, Widget, Agent Worker, SFC, modules, resources, packaging, TypeScript, `offload`, or single-file Source updates.
- Read [events.md](./references/events.md) for lifecycle, interaction, key, focus, voice wakeup, head gesture, and environment-awareness events.
- Read [components.md](./references/components.md) before using or reviewing built-in components and their attributes or events.
- Read [wxss.md](./references/wxss.md) before writing styles, layout, selectors, animation, or custom fonts.
- For keyframes, animation events, text-triggered decorations, or 2D transforms, also read [animation.md](./references/animation.md).
- Read [monochrome-green.md](./references/design/monochrome-green.md) only for the monochrome-green Rokid Glasses visual language.
- Read [full-color.md](./references/design/full-color.md) for the Rokid Color full-color visual language and adaptive layouts.
- Read [APIs index](./references/apis/index.md), then its matching domain file, before using runtime APIs.
- For recording source selection or microphone modes, read [media APIs](./references/apis/media.md#recording-source-and-microphone-mode).
- For Widget or Agent Worker instance methods, read [Widget API](./references/apis/widget.md) or [Agent Worker API](./references/apis/agent-worker.md).
- Read and apply [delivery checklist](./references/checklist.md) before declaring a generated or modified AIUI agent complete.
- Start from the matching scaffold when useful: [minimal Page](./assets/minimal-page.ink), [minimal Widget](./assets/minimal-widget.ink), or [minimal Agent Worker](./assets/minimal-agent-worker.js).

Do not load every reference for a narrow task. For example, an Agent Worker normally needs `framework.md`, `events.md`, and `apis/agent-worker.md`, but not Canvas or the full component catalog.

## Core Authoring Rules

- Register App, Page, Widget, Component, and Agent Worker logic with `export default { ... }`; do not use `App()`, `Page()`, `Widget()`, or similar registration functions.
- Use either a multi-file Page or a single `.ink` Page for one route, never both.
- A `.ink` Page uses `<script def>`, `<script setup>`, `<page>`, and `<style>`. A Widget replaces `<page>` with `<widget>`.
- Declare every Page, Widget, Agent Worker, and custom component in the appropriate configuration before using it.
- Declare required capabilities in `app.json.permissions`; handle device authorization failures separately.
- Treat Widget `family` as a size category. Use relative layout and never hardcode the root to the current Glasses pixel size.
- Use `agentWorkers`, not the removed `workers` field. Extend asynchronous `onOpen` work synchronously with `event.waitUntil(promise)`.
- Use data binding for rendered state and `this.setData()` to update it.
- Page `onReady()` and component `lifetimes.ready()` run once per instance after their first visible frame is presented; parsing or layout completion alone is insufficient.
- Resolve packaged resources from project paths; do not invent filesystem or network access that the target does not expose.
- Treat conversation-flow cards as display-only unless the task explicitly targets an interactive full-screen Page or Widget.

## Target and Design Choice

Before styling, determine the intended surface:

- Conversation-flow card: compact, display-only information.
- Full-screen Page: interactive agent UI.
- Widget: compact `1x1` or `1x2` surface with Widget lifecycle.
- Monochrome-green Rokid Glasses: apply `design/monochrome-green.md` after the general WXSS rules.
- Rokid Color: apply `design/full-color.md` after the general WXSS rules.
- Other displays: use theme tokens and task requirements; do not automatically apply the monochrome-green visual language.

## Runtime API Workflow

1. Open [references/apis/index.md](./references/apis/index.md) and select the domain.
2. Confirm the exact constructor or method, parameters, return type, events, errors, permissions, and lifecycle in that domain reference.
3. If the API is absent or the requested overload is not documented, inspect current Ink types or implementation rather than guessing.
4. Keep capability checks and cleanup close to the code that acquires the resource.

## Completion Checks

Run the [AIUI agent delivery checklist](./references/checklist.md). Report which executable checks ran, what they proved, and any target-device behavior that remains unverified. Do not call an agent runnable only because its files look structurally correct.

title: Package size accounting and delivery
content:
# Package size accounting and delivery

## Inventory and prioritization

- For a supplied spreadsheet, find the real size column and units, apply the threshold to byte values, count excluded boundary cases, and report downloads that fail or differ from recorded sizes. Inspect each selected archive before describing its contents.
- For each archive, record its original total, major files/categories, compressed and uncompressed entry sizes, and source location. ZIP entry compressed sizes determine current package contributions; category classification by extension is approximate and archive overhead is separate.
- First list each package containing suspected nested builds, backups, cache, previews, logs, test artifacts, or developer-only materials. Show each cleanup item and its current compressed bytes, the package's original and estimated cleanup-only size, plus counts and non-overlapping totals across packages and the full population. Keep this subtotal separate from image optimization and later downloads.
- For every selected package, include concrete major contributors and actions, original size, local-only outcome, first-install size if optional resources are moved, and deferred transfer for the defined scenario. If no actionable measurement was made for a package, keep its measured size unchanged and say what remains to investigate. Show actual image dimensions and target display sizes when known.
- Classify every measured package against the required **≤ 2 MiB** limit and recommended **≤ 1 MiB** target, and summarize counts in all three statuses defined in `SKILL.md`. Separately identify predicted and verified outcomes; for a package above a boundary, show the bytes that must still be saved to reach it. Use full package-file bytes and do not round before comparing.

## Size outcomes

- Prefer actual rebuilt archive bytes; identify the exact source, tool and options, and check that all required functionality and AIX metadata survived. Without a build, label an outcome as an estimate and state each assumption.
- An optimized package over 2 MiB fails the required limit even if it is much smaller than before. A package at or under 2 MiB but over 1 MiB meets the requirement and misses the recommendation. Unbuilt or unmeasured packages have unknown final status, even if their estimated sizes are below either boundary.
- A cleanup-only estimate can subtract the compressed bytes of distinct excluded entries from original archive bytes; ZIP directory/manifest changes make this approximate. For a re-encoded image, compare the entry's previous compressed contribution with the new encoded contribution under the assumed packaging method. Do not subtract an entry once for cleanup and again for resizing or deferral.
- For on-demand loading, report initial package bytes separately from the bytes of the selected remote resources downloaded once. Use actual encoded remote file bytes, or clearly state HTTP/content-encoding assumptions; compressed ZIP bytes are not automatically equal to transfer bytes. Include startup assets, added loader/index bytes, cache occupancy, HTTP overhead, repeated downloads, and offline fallback if known; mark excluded or unknown costs explicitly. First-install reduction is not necessarily a reduction in total traffic or device storage.
- Record the tested or estimated image bounds and transformations, audio codec and parameters, data partitioning, changed paths, and any quality or feature trade-offs. Do not assert a target size is achieved merely because file-level arithmetic predicts it.

## Validation

Run relevant project checks and compare old/new package inventories. Verify package metadata, generated manifest and integrity/signatures using the project's available tooling; exercise changed static and dynamic references and representative startup and deferred flows. Check offline, slow or failed downloads, fallback, cache invalidation and quota when introduced. Where applicable, validate image crop and sharpness, sprite coordinates, audio timing and quality, device decode support, and behavior on the intended device. Report precisely what was and was not tested; keep unrelated changes untouched.

title: audit_aix.py
AIUI Package Optimization
content:
---
name: aiui-optimize
description: Audit, measure, and optimize AIUI agent and AIX package size, including release contents, image and audio assets, and on-demand resource loading. Use for package size investigations or implementing size reductions in AIUI projects.
---

# AIUI Package Optimization

Identify what makes each package large, then implement and measure authorized optimizations. Respect the user's scope: an audit is read-only; a request to optimize includes appropriate source and build changes. Do not upload assets, publish packages, or change remote services without authorization for that action.

## Package size requirements

Each released AIX package must be **at most 2 MiB (2,097,152 bytes)**. The recommended target is **at most 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes)**. These limits apply to the actual complete package file, including ZIP and AIX metadata, not the sum of extracted files. For resources moved out of the package, assess the package itself against these limits and report later transfer and cache storage separately.

Classify each measured package using byte values: over 2 MiB is **over the required limit**; over 1 MiB and at most 2 MiB **meets the limit but exceeds the recommended target**; at most 1 MiB **meets the recommended target**. Values exactly on either boundary satisfy that boundary. A report filter may narrow which packages are analyzed, but must not be confused with these requirements.

When executing optimization, work toward the 1 MiB recommendation while meeting the 2 MiB limit. Verify the final built artifact's bytes: a projection is not proof of compliance. If the actual package remains over 2 MiB or cannot be rebuilt or measured, report it explicitly and do not claim the size requirement is met. If it meets 2 MiB but not 1 MiB, report that distinction and the remaining gap.

## Establish the baseline

1. Identify the input: AIUI source, `.aix` package(s), or an inventory with package paths and sizes. Preserve unrelated changes. If only an inventory is available, distinguish its totals from inspected archive contents; report inaccessible or size-mismatched packages. Apply the size requirements above in bytes; respect a separately requested analysis filter and distinguish MB from MiB. For spreadsheets, use the available spreadsheet workflow.
2. Measure actual package bytes and inspect archive entries, including compressed and uncompressed sizes. AIX is ZIP-based; a raw ZIP edit is not a valid replacement for the AIX build and integrity workflow. Do not extract an untrusted archive blindly. The standard-library helper below inventories local archives without extracting them:

   ```bash
   python3 /path/to/aiui-optimize/scripts/audit_aix.py app.aix --screen 480x352 > inventory.json
   ```

   Resolve the helper path relative to this skill. `--screen` is optional; use the actual target viewport, not a universal fixed resolution. The helper reports candidate paths, image headers, and exact content duplicates; it cannot prove usage, safe removal, or runtime behavior.
3. Rank entries by compressed contribution and inspect manifests, actual references, dynamic path construction, rendering code, startup paths, and build rules. Record uncertainty, including files that are unreachable, invalid, unsupported, or larger than the duplicate hash limit. Do not expose access-bearing URLs or credentials in the report.

## Choose and execute optimizations

Prioritize release contents, then oversized assets, then optional remote resources. Put packages with suspected release-only clutter first and total their distinct removable bytes; do not count duplicates, exclusions, recompression, or remote movement twice. A matching filename or absent static reference is a lead, not proof of safe removal. Preserve application entrypoints, required runtime resources, `AGENTS.md` where required, and applicable license/attribution files. Prefer scoped `.aixignore` rules or build configuration to deleting source files.

- **Images:** compare intrinsic dimensions with the actual display container, fit/crop mode, scaling, target pixel density, and any other use. For the 480×352 target, use that size as a viewport only when applicable; icons can be much smaller. Do not blindly resize a sprite sheet, glyph atlas, tiled/scrolling image, zoomable image, or a sample used for vision. Preserve transparency and compatible formats. Measure candidate encoded bytes and validate visual quality; update atlas coordinates and references if dimensions change.
- **Audio and data:** inspect duration, channels, sample rate, encoding, usage, and device support before transcoding. Keep latency-sensitive effects and startup-critical data available locally. Consider splitting large maps, datasets, image collections, and optional music by use; retain a functional default and offline fallback where needed.
- **On-demand resources:** specify exactly what remains in the package, what is fetched, when it is fetched, and what happens without network. Verify the current AIUI version and playback path: image and Audio Player may accept network URLs, while `Sound` is documented for local files. Do not assume an OPFS file can be passed to a player. Account for cache availability and quota, timeouts, retries, versioning, integrity, cleanup, and repeated downloads. Remote code/data loading may require restructuring rather than changing a path.
- **Build and integrity:** inspect the project's AIX tooling and current `.aixignore` semantics. When available, evaluate `aix pack --optimize` or `aix optimize` against the actual inputs; they do not replace workload-specific resizing or splitting. Rebuild through the supported AIX workflow so the manifest, entry digests, identity, and any required signatures remain valid. Never present a manually modified ZIP as a verified AIX.

For media transformation, try a representative sample before changing a whole class. Preserve original formats and behavior unless the task authorizes a change and compatibility is verified. If the user requested execution, make the viable changes and run appropriate checks rather than stopping at recommendations; report anything blocked by missing source, tooling, hosting, or device access.

## Measure and report

Read [reporting.md](references/reporting.md) for multi-package reporting, estimate accounting, and validation. Present release-content cleanup first, followed by every in-scope package, with original size and size status, main contributors, proposed or completed changes, local and optional first-install size and status, and deferred transfer. Separate actual builds and measurements from theoretical estimates, and distinguish package-size savings from bytes later transferred. Validate affected functionality, resource references and package integrity; report device, visual, audio, offline, or network checks that were not run.

title: test_audit_aix.py
content:
import hashlib
import io
import json
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path


SCRIPT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "scripts" / "audit_aix.py"
MIB = 1024 * 1024


def zip_bytes(entries):
    output = io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(output, "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_STORED) as archive:
        for name, data in entries:
            archive.writestr(name, data)
    return output.getvalue()


def png_header(width, height):
    return b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + struct.pack(">I", 13) + b"IHDR" + struct.pack(">II", width, height)


class AuditAixTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
        self.directory = Path(self.tmp.name)

    def run_audit(self, *arguments):
        return subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, str(SCRIPT), *map(str, arguments)],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=False,
        )

    def test_inventories_without_modifying_archive(self):
        image = png_header(1254, 1254)
        entries = [
            ("AGENTS.md", b"instructions"),
            ("docs/NOTICE.md", b"attribution"),
            ("docs/plan.md", b"development plan"),
            ("assets/logos.bak-2026/logo.png", image),
            ("assets/logo.png", image),
            ("assets/sprite.png", png_header(768, 96)),
            ("code/a.js", b"same content"),
            ("code/b.js", b"same content"),
            ("../unsafe", b"not extracted"),
        ]
        package = self.directory / "sample.aix"
        package.write_bytes(zip_bytes(entries))
        before = hashlib.sha256(package.read_bytes()).digest()

        result = self.run_audit(package, "--screen", "480x352")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        report = json.loads(result.stdout)["archives"][0]
        self.assertEqual(report["archive_bytes"], package.stat().st_size)
        self.assertEqual(report["entry_count"], len(entries))
        self.assertEqual(
            report["entry_compressed_bytes"] + report["archive_overhead_bytes"],
            report["archive_bytes"],
        )
        candidates = {item["path"] for item in report["release_cleanup_candidates"]}
        self.assertIn("docs/plan.md", candidates)
        self.assertIn("assets/logos.bak-2026/logo.png", candidates)
        self.assertNotIn("docs/NOTICE.md", candidates)
        self.assertNotIn("AGENTS.md", candidates)
        images = {item["path"]: item for item in report["images"]}
        self.assertEqual((images["assets/logo.png"]["width"], images["assets/logo.png"]["height"]), (1254, 1254))
        self.assertEqual((images["assets/sprite.png"]["width"], images["assets/sprite.png"]["height"]), (768, 96))
        self.assertTrue(images["assets/sprite.png"]["exceeds_viewport"])
        duplicate_paths = [set(group["paths"]) for group in report["duplicate_groups"]]
        self.assertIn({"code/a.js", "code/b.js"}, duplicate_paths)
        self.assertIn({"assets/logo.png", "assets/logos.bak-2026/logo.png"}, duplicate_paths)
        self.assertEqual(report["unsafe_entry_names"], ["../unsafe"])
        self.assertEqual(report["inspection_errors"], [])
        self.assertEqual(hashlib.sha256(package.read_bytes()).digest(), before)

    def test_size_limit_boundaries(self):
        overhead = len(zip_bytes([("x", b"")]))
        cases = [
            (MIB - 1, "within_recommended"),
            (MIB, "within_recommended"),
            (MIB + 1, "within_limit_above_recommended"),
            (2 * MIB, "within_limit_above_recommended"),
            (2 * MIB + 1, "over_required_limit"),
        ]
        paths = []
        for size, _ in cases:
            path = self.directory / str(size)
            path.write_bytes(zip_bytes([("x", bytes(size - overhead))]))
            self.assertEqual(path.stat().st_size, size)
            paths.append(path)

        result = self.run_audit(*paths)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        for report, (size, expected) in zip(json.loads(result.stdout)["archives"], cases):
            self.assertEqual(report["size_status"], expected)
            self.assertEqual(report["bytes_over_required_limit"], max(0, size - 2 * MIB))
            self.assertEqual(report["bytes_over_recommended_target"], max(0, size - MIB))

    def test_hash_limit_and_invalid_archive(self):
        package = self.directory / "sample.aix"
        package.write_bytes(zip_bytes([("a", b"same"), ("b", b"same")]))
        result = self.run_audit(package, "--hash-limit-mib", "0")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
        report = json.loads(result.stdout)["archives"][0]
        self.assertEqual(report["duplicate_groups"], [])
        self.assertEqual(set(report["duplicate_hash_skipped_paths"]), {"a", "b"})

        invalid = self.directory / "invalid.aix"
        invalid.write_bytes(b"not a ZIP")
        result = self.run_audit(package, invalid)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertIn("error", json.loads(result.stdout)["archives"][1])
        self.assertEqual(self.run_audit(package, "--screen", "0x352").returncode, 2)

    def test_unsupported_compression_is_reported(self):
        package = self.directory / "unsupported.aix"
        data = bytearray(zip_bytes([("image.png", png_header(10, 10))]))
        local = data.index(b"PK\x03\x04")
        central = data.index(b"PK\x01\x02")
        struct.pack_into("<H", data, local + 8, 99)
        struct.pack_into("<H", data, central + 10, 99)
        package.write_bytes(data)

        result = self.run_audit(package)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        errors = json.loads(result.stdout)["archives"][0]["inspection_errors"]
        self.assertEqual(errors[0]["operation"], "image_header")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
